CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99214
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/vc4: hdmi: Move packet RAM enable to PM runtime

Audio can be triggered by the HPD handler and start up before video has
been restored, calling vc4_hdmi_write_infoframe() for the audio infoframe.
vc4_hdmi_write_infoframe() needs Packet RAM to be on to store the
infoframe, however, if the video hasn't been enabled,
vc4_hdmi_encoder_post_crtc_enable() hasn't been called and therefore, the
Packet RAM can be disabled by the time vc4_hdmi_write_infoframe() executes,
causing the following splat:

[  201.570266] ------------[ cut here ]------------
[  201.570293] Packet RAM has to be on to store the packet.
[  201.570367] WARNING: drivers/gpu/drm/vc4/vc4_hdmi.c:683 at vc4_hdmi_write_infoframe+0x404/0x494 [vc4], CPU#0: wireplumber/1606
[...]
[  201.658650] Hardware name: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B Rev 1.5 (DT)
[...]
[  201.758499] Call trace:
[  201.760967]  vc4_hdmi_write_infoframe+0x404/0x494 [vc4] (P)
[  201.766607]  vc4_hdmi_write_audio_infoframe+0x1c/0x28 [vc4]
[  201.772247]  write_infoframe+0xbc/0x140 [drm_display_helper]
[  201.777975]  drm_atomic_helper_connector_hdmi_update_audio_infoframe+0x80/0xdc [drm_display_helper]
[  201.787140]  vc4_hdmi_audio_prepare+0x4ac/0x570 [vc4]
[  201.792252]  drm_connector_hdmi_audio_prepare+0x24/0x30 [drm_display_helper]
[  201.799390]  hdmi_codec_prepare+0x100/0x160 [snd_soc_hdmi_codec]
[  201.805471]  snd_soc_pcm_dai_prepare+0xd4/0x100 [snd_soc_core]
[  201.811375]  __soc_pcm_prepare+0x60/0x12c [snd_soc_core]
[  201.816752]  soc_pcm_prepare+0x34/0x58 [snd_soc_core]
[  201.821863]  snd_pcm_do_prepare+0x70/0x8c [snd_pcm]
[  201.826798]  snd_pcm_action_nonatomic+0xe4/0x174 [snd_pcm]
[  201.832350]  snd_pcm_prepare+0xc8/0xd8 [snd_pcm]
[  201.837021]  snd_pcm_common_ioctl+0x458/0x614 [snd_pcm]
[  201.842308]  snd_pcm_ioctl+0x30/0x48 [snd_pcm]
[  201.846802]  __arm64_sys_ioctl+0x88/0xd8
[  201.850769]  invoke_syscall+0x48/0xf4
[  201.854470]  el0_svc_common+0x80/0xd8
[  201.858171]  do_el0_svc+0x1c/0x28
[  201.861520]  el0_svc+0x3c/0xb0
[  201.864605]  el0t_64_sync_handler+0x68/0xdc
[  201.868834]  el0t_64_sync+0x198/0x19c
[  201.872536] ---[ end trace 0000000000000000 ]---

Considering that Packet RAM enable is essentially a power management
configuration, move its enabling/disabling to the Runtime PM hooks.

Note that post_crtc_disable() still stops all infoframes, but keeps Packet
RAM enabled, leaving it to be disabled by runtime suspend.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99213
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vsock: treat TCP_CLOSING as once-established

Handle the TCP_ESTABLISHED -> TCP_CLOSING transition on OP_RST, which can
race with the connect loop. Immediately break and return 0 on
ESTABLISHED/CLOSING. The return value of connect() should reflect what
happened up to the point the connection was established or failed. Events
that occur afterwards must not affect it. E.g. even if OP_RW has already
set sk_err, connect() should still return 0, not ENOBUFS because of it.
Adapt the inaccurate comment above signal_pending().

Resetting a socket that is still present in connected_table can lead to
memory corruption. The reporter noted lost transports for in-flight skbs,
and I have reproduced crashes caused by re-insertion into connected_table.

  list_add double add: new=, prev=, next=.
  kernel BUG at lib/list_debug.c:35!
  Oops: invalid opcode: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
  Workqueue: vsock-loopback vsock_loopback_work
  RIP: 0010:__list_add_valid_or_report+0x11f/0x130
  Call Trace:
   vsock_insert_connected.cold+0xe/0x13
   virtio_transport_recv_pkt+0x10e9/0x1460
   vsock_loopback_work+0x305/0x480
   process_one_work+0xe4c/0x1560
   worker_thread+0x4f1/0xd60
   kthread+0x36e/0x470
   ret_from_fork+0x47b/0x6b0
   ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30

This fix is supplementary to commit 002541ef650b ("vsock: Ignore
signal/timeout on connect() if already established"). Details under Link.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99212
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/rds: don't let the rdma_cm destroy an id RDS still owns on route failure

rds_rdma_cm_event_handler_cmn() hands the return value of
rdma_resolve_route() straight back to the rdma_cm on
RDMA_CM_EVENT_ADDR_RESOLVED.  A synchronous failure there - -ENOMEM
from the route work allocation, an SA query that cannot be set up, a
RoCE route with no usable device - makes addr_handler() destroy the
id the event was delivered on.  That id is ic->i_cm_id, and nothing
clears the pointer: the connection sits in RDS_CONN_CONNECTING with a
freed id until its shutdown calls rdma_disconnect() and
rdma_destroy_id() on it.

The ROUTE_RESOLVED case already avoids this: rds_ib_cm_initiate_connect()
forces a zero return while ic->i_cm_id == cm_id, as the comment there
explains.  Do the same here - drop the connection and return 0 - so
the id stays RDS's to destroy from the shutdown, and the reconnect
gets a fresh one.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99211
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netlink: reset skb headers before unicast and multicast filtering

Socket filters can use SKF_NET_OFF and SKF_LL_OFF to read relative to
an skb's network and MAC headers. Netlink producers may reserve
headroom without resetting those headers, allowing a receiving socket's
filter to read data before the initialized message.

For example, IWPM HELLO replies are allocated with dev_alloc_skb(),
which reserves NET_SKB_PAD bytes. An unprivileged NETLINK_RDMA user can
attach a classic socket filter and disclose this headroom through the
length of the delivered reply. The resets in netlink_dump() do not help
because IWPM sends a separately allocated skb through netlink_unicast().

Reset both headers before running the receiver's filter in unicast and
broadcast delivery, as is already done for dump skbs. This also covers
other netlink producers that reserve headroom without changing their
allocation or message-building code.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99210
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

accel/rocket: clear rdev on device init failure

rocket_probe() stores the return value from rocket_device_init() in the
file-scoped rdev pointer before checking whether it is an error pointer.
If rocket_device_init() fails, rdev is left as an ERR_PTR.

The rdev pointer is also used as the marker for whether the shared rocket
device has already been initialized. A later core probe can therefore see
a non-NULL rdev, skip rocket_device_init(), and dereference the error
pointer when reading rdev->num_cores.

Save the error code and clear rdev before returning from the
rocket_device_init() failure path.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99209
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/xe: skip eviction of a BO with no resource

xe_evict_flags() switches on tbo->resource->mem_type to choose an
eviction placement. An xe BO can reach eviction with no ttm.resource,
e.g. an imported dma-buf BO whose resource was freed during teardown
while its attachment is still live: the exporter then invalidates it via
xe_dma_buf_move_notify() -> xe_bo_evict(), and the switch dereferences a
NULL resource and faults.

A BO with no resource has nothing placed or mapped, so there is nothing
to evict. Return an empty placement (num_placement = 0), mirroring the
handling already used for non-xe scatter-gather BOs just above;
ttm_bo_validate() then takes the pipeline-gutting path and returns 0.

Without the fix the xe_dma_buf@xe_test_dmabuf_move_notify_no_resource
dynamic live selftest will fail with below stack.

BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000010
RIP: 0010:xe_evict_flags+0xf4/0x140 [xe]
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 xe_bo_evict+0x40/0xa0 [xe]
 ? ttm_bo_pipeline_gutting+0x71/0x180 [ttm]
 xe_test_dmabuf_move_notify_no_resource+0x182/0x440 [xe]
 xe_dma_buf_kunit+0x387/0x580 [xe]

v2: Add Fixes tag and failure info in commit text (Matt Brost)

(cherry picked from commit dbcfaac6331f1fcb0c2fe3ad3e9adb1e5d43ec0c)

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99208
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/xe/oa: Zero OA buffer at allocation

ttm_bo_type_kernel BOs are not guaranteed to be zeroed on allocation and
may contain data from previously freed pages. Since the OA buffer is
mmap'able by userspace, this can expose stale kernel memory contents.

Streams opened with DRM_XE_OA_PROPERTY_OA_DISABLED allocate the OA
buffer without calling xe_oa_init_oa_buffer(). Zero the buffer at
allocation to prevent information disclosure through mmap.

The existing zeroing in xe_oa_init_oa_buffer() remains necessary for
zero report-id/timestamp detection on enable/re-enable.

(cherry picked from commit 126c4c5388f9311a390b9b254a835b0cf0f55331)

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99207
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: target: Disable interrupts while holding delayed_cmd_lock

target_do_delayed_work() takes dev->delayed_cmd_lock with a plain
spin_lock(). It runs from system_percpu_wq, so interrupts stay enabled
while the lock is held. Every other acquisition of that lock uses
spin_lock_irqsave(): target_handle_task_attr() and
transport_complete_ordered_sync() in target_core_transport.c, and
target_non_ordered_release() in target_core_device.c.

That was safe while every caller of transport_complete_task_attr() ran
in process context: target_complete_ok_work() from target_completion_wq,
transport_complete_qf() from dev->qf_work_queue, and
transport_generic_request_failure() from the submit and execute paths.

Since commit 06933066d88a ("scsi: target: Add support for completing
commands from backend context") that is no longer true. With
complete_type=1 on a fabric that sets direct_compl_supp,
target_complete() runs target_complete_ok_work() inline in the backend's
completion context, which target_complete_cmd_with_sense() documents as
"May be called from interrupt context". For iblock that is the bio
end_io.

target_complete_ok_work() starts with transport_complete_task_attr(),
which takes delayed_cmd_lock in two ways:

 - Every ORDERED command is put on dev->delayed_cmd_list by
   target_handle_task_attr() and dispatched from there by
   target_do_delayed_work(), which marks it SCF_TASK_ORDERED_SYNC.  Its
   completion therefore goes through transport_complete_ordered_sync().

 - A SIMPLE command that completes while an ORDERED command is pending
   drops the last reference to the killed dev->non_ordered, and
   percpu_ref_put() then runs target_non_ordered_release() in the
   completing context.

Both take the lock and, if commands are waiting, call
schedule_work(&dev->delayed_cmd_work), which queues on system_percpu_wq,
i.e. on the CPU that took the completion. Further completions for the
same queue are typically delivered there too, so one arriving while the
work holds the lock spins on it forever.

Reaching this needs complete_type=1, which is not the default
(vhost-scsi, the only fabric with direct_compl_supp, defaults to
TARGET_QUEUE_COMPL), a backend whose I/O completes from interrupt
context, and ORDERED commands from the initiator. Linux virtio_scsi
guests send only VIRTIO_SCSI_S_SIMPLE and never take the ordered path;
any guest that uses the ORDERED task attribute, which vhost-scsi
accepts, does.

target_do_delayed_work() is a work item and always runs in process
context, so spin_lock_irq() is sufficient.

Found by inspection; no runtime report. A single ORDERED command goes
through both acquisitions, so with CONFIG_PROVE_LOCKING the first one
completed through direct completion should produce an inconsistent lock
state report on delayed_cmd_lock (hardirq or softirq, depending on where
the backend completes).

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99206
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: target: iscsi: Fix race in discovery auth updates

Separate configfs opens can concurrently update the discovery AuthMethod
parameter. Both callers may free the same value in
iscsi_update_param_value(), causing a double-free.

Protect the lookup and replacement with the discovery TPG access lock,
as used by the other TPG configfs parameter updates.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99205
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sched/core: Call wakeup_preempt() for queued tasks during class change

Paul reported recent RCU changes exposed a lost resched where CPU idles
with a rcutorture thread waiting while being completely runnable.

Dumping the rq state at the time of idling with runnable tasks showed
the following:

  rq->next_class = &fair_sched_class
  rq->nr_running = 1
  rq->cfs.h_nr_queued = 0
  rq->rt.rt_nr_running = 1

Although the waiting task was an RT task, "rq->next_class" did not point
to rt_sched_class and was stuck at the lower priority fair_sched_class.

Inspecting sched_change_end() revealed the following race with
__sched_setscheduler() for queued, but non-running tasks:

    CPU0                                   CPU1
    ====                                   ====

  __schedule()

    /*
     * rq->donor is a fair task that blocks.
     * rq->next_class = &fair_sched_class
     */

    rq_lock(rq0)

    pick_next_task()
      /* nr_running = 0 */
      pick_task_fair()
        sched_balance_newidle()
          raw_spin_rq_unlock(rq0)
                                    rq_lock(rq0)

                                    activate_task(rq0, p)
                                      /* p is a fair task */
                                      rq0->nr_running++;
                                      rq0->cfs.h_nr_queued++;
                                      wakeup_preempt(rq, p)
                                        rq->next_class = &fair_sched_class
                                        resched_curr()

                                    rq_unlock(rq0)

                                    __sched_setscheduler(p)
                                      /* p is moved to SCHED_RR */
                                      task_rq_lock(p)
                                      sched_change_begin()

				      rq0->cfs.h_nr_queued--;
				      rq0->rt.rt_nr_running++;

                                      sched_change_end()
                                        /*
                                         * p->on_rq = 1 (ctx->queued)
                                         * but p is not rq->donor
                                         * (!ctx->running) hence
                                         * resched_curr() is and
                                         * rq->next_class upgrade is
                                         * skipped.
                                         */

                                       task_rq_unlock()

          raw_spin_rq_lock(rq0)

          /*
           * rq->nr_running = 1
           * rq->cfs.h_nr_queued = 0
           * rq->rt.rt_nr_running = 1
           * rq->next_class = &fair_sched_class
           */

           if (rq->cfs.h_nr_queued && ...)
             /* Above is false */

           if (rq_modified_above(this_rq, &fair_sched_class))
             /* Also false since rq->next_class is still fair */

      /*
       * sched_balance_newidle() is considered to
       * have failed to pull any fair tasks and no
       * other wakeups were detected.
       */
       return NULL; /* pick_task_fair() */

    pick_task_idle()
      return rq->idle;

    next = rq->idle;

    /* Preemption indicators are lost */
    clear_tsk_need_resched(prev);
    clear_preempt_need_resched();

    rq->curr = rq->idle;

  !!! rq->idle switches in with rq->running == 1 but !need_resched() !!!

In simple words, enqueue, followed by a class change of the newly queued
task goes unnoticed in rq->next_class indicator and
sched_balance_newidle() sees no fair task, nor any higher priority task
enqueued.

The above sequence will lead to CPU idling with a runnable task on the
CPU.

Call wakeup_preempt() for ctx->queued cases in sched_change_end() to
re-evaluate rq->next_class after class change (ENQUEUE_CLASS) and set
the NEED_RESCHED indicator accordingly.

Newidle balance will correctly see an enqueue of a higher priority
t
---truncated---

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-115522
CVE.report.description: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere (CWE-668) in FileArtifactService in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Python (google-adk) versions 1.19.0 before 1.39.1 and 2.0.0a1 before 2.7.0 allows a caller in one application to list, read, overwrite, or delete artifacts belonging to another application when both applications share a FileArtifactService root directory and use the same user_id (and session_id for session-scoped artifacts). FileArtifactService accepted app_name across its public API methods but omitted app_name when constructing on-disk paths (root/users/{user_id}/... instead of root/apps/{app_name}/users/{user_id}/...). Version 2.6.0 scoped writes by app_name but retained a legacy root/users/{user_id} fallback for reads and deletes; version 2.7.0 and the 1.x backport in version 1.39.1 removed the fallback and enforce full per-app path scoping.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-104384
CVE.report.description: Insufficiently Protected Credentials in tunnel gateway and provisioning interfaces in EagleCloud Aquila versions through 2.6.7.2 on on-premises platforms allows unauthenticated remote attackers to escalate privileges via authentication abuse to access the access keys, secret keys, and deployment secrets

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-104383
CVE.report.description: Improper Control of Generation of Code in Pigeon MFA service in EagleCloud Aquila versions through 2.6.7.2 on on-premises platforms allows authenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via code injection

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-111497
CVE.report.description:
A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.





Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118276
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability was determined in a2ui-project a2ui up to 0.10.6. This vulnerability affects the function formatString of the file renderers/web_core/src/v0_9/basic_catalog/expressions/expression_parser.ts of the component Parser. This manipulation causes resource consumption. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. Patch name: 1f71d1aac1b145ef57c7526f9e0cff316f5934e2. Applying a patch is the recommended action to fix this issue.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118275
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability was found in a2ui-project a2ui up to 0.10.6. This affects the function DataContext.resolveSignal of the file renderers/web_core/src/v0_9/rendering/data-context.ts of the component Resolver. The manipulation results in resource consumption. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The patch is identified as c76e17272e52c12c6dcf68905b1df978c39e9aa5. It is advisable to implement a patch to correct this issue.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118008
CVE.report.description: Privilege escalation in the DOM: Navigation component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 159 and Thunderbird 159.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116613
CVE.report.description: The Animated Text Block plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in versions up to, and including, 1.2.6 via the 'animated-text' shortcode. This is due to the atb_shortcode_handler() function fetching an arbitrary post by attacker-supplied ID and, in the 'publish' branch, calling displayContent() with no capability check and no validation that the post's post_type is the plugin's own CPT or is otherwise viewable (is_post_type_viewable()). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to read the rendered block content of any published post, including posts of non-public custom post types (public=false, show_in_rest=false) that WordPress would otherwise hide from direct URLs and the REST API.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-111727
CVE.report.description: The Appointment Booking Calendar plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'vs_text_submitbtn' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.05 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the attacker to be assigned as a calendar owner, a per-user grant that any administrator can extend to users as low as Subscriber level through the plugin's calendar list screen. Exploitation by attackers with subscriber-level access and above requires that an administrator has assigned the attacker's account as owner (`conwer`) of a calendar via the plugin's calendar list screen; the plugin's UI lists all registered users regardless of role, so a Subscriber can be assigned. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with editor-level access and above.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-111255
CVE.report.description: The affiliate-toolkit – Multi-Network Affiliate & Amazon Product Display plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 3.9.2 via the upload_image function. This is due to insufficient file type validation in upload_image due to a weak Content-Type prefix check and extension derivation from the attacker-controlled URL path, with no dangerous-extension stripping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. Exploitation requires the "import product image" option to be enabled in the plugin settings, as this activates the image download pipeline triggered on product post save.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99100
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: p54: validate firmware record lengths

The p54 firmware parser accesses component ID and component version
records without checking that their lengths cover the fields being read.
A malformed record can therefore make the parser read past the record.

Validate the component ID and component version record lengths before
accessing their data. The descriptor record is also checked against the
shortest descriptor length found in the supported firmware images.

Reject descriptor values that underflow the RX offset or produce an empty
RX range before updating the driver state.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-1928
CVE.report.description: The Rank Math SEO – AI SEO Tools to Dominate SEO Rankings plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.276 via deserialization of untrusted input in the updateMeta REST API endpoint. This makes it possible forauthenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject a PHP Object. The additional presence of a POP chain allows attackers to achieve remote code execution by writing a webshell to the uploads directory.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-48356
CVE.report.description: Adobe Commerce is affected by an Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type vulnerability that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user, potentially gaining elevated access or control over the victim's account or session. Exploitation of this issue requires user interaction in that a victim must visit a maliciously crafted URL or interact with a compromised web page. Scope is changed.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118384
CVE.report.description: GNU mtools through 4.0.49 has an out-of-bounds write in parse_vses in vfat.c.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-97019
CVE.report.description: The AMP for WP – Accelerated Mobile Pages plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'headline-*' Shortcode Attribute in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.17 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A Subscriber-level user can store a malicious shortcode in their biographical info field; because WordPress core's wp_filter_kses() only strips HTML tags and not shortcode syntax, and because AMP content sanitizers run before do_shortcode() processes the archive description, the synthesized markup is never post-sanitized.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-84999
CVE.report.description: The Pie Register Premium plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Unrestricted File Type Upload in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.4.0 via the piereg_file_upload function. This is due to the plugin performing file type validation via wp_check_filetype and wp_check_filetype_and_ext but never checking whether those validation calls produced errors before move_uploaded_file() is called, combined with no nonce or capability check on the AJAX handler. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files of dangerous types (e.g. PHP scripts) that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. The server returns the generated destination filename in the response, giving the attacker the exact path needed to trigger the uploaded file.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118378
CVE.report.description: Tabularis before 0.28.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its SQLite driver that allows MCP clients to execute stacked statements by supplying a crafted table_name to the describe_table tool. Attackers, including AI agents steered by untrusted content, can close the quoted PRAGMA argument and append statements to read, modify, or drop SQLite data, bypassing read-only mode and write approval.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118377
CVE.report.description: mews/pos through 2.0.0 contains an insufficient verification of data authenticity vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge payment results by submitting unverified callbacks. GarantiPos, PayForPos and InterPos 3D Pay and 3D Host handlers skip check3DHash(), letting attackers post tampered status, amount or order ID fields to complete orders without paying.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118376
CVE.report.description: WeKnora before 0.8.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in isRestrictedIP() that misclassifies NAT64-prefixed IPv6 addresses as public. Authenticated attackers can supply URLs resolving to NAT64 encodings of internal addresses via web_fetch or URL-based knowledge import to reach internal services or cloud metadata endpoints.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118375
CVE.report.description: llama.cpp b8841 before b11865 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the ggml-rpc RDMA transport rdma_recv() function that allows unauthenticated peers to overflow the rpc-server stack. Attackers advertising RDMA capabilities in the HELLO message can send up to 256 KiB into a 1-byte stack variable in rpc_serve_client(), crashing the server or potentially executing code.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118374
CVE.report.description: LibreSSL ocspcheck through 4.4.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability that allows malicious OCSP responders to exhaust memory by sending unbounded HTTP responses. Attackers controlling the responder or intercepting plain HTTP AIA OCSP traffic can stream endless headers or body data to http_head_read() and http_body_read(), denying certificate status checks.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118373
CVE.report.description: LibreSSL ocspcheck through 4.4.0 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability because url2host() discards the OCSP URL scheme and http_alloc() only selects TLS for port 443. On-path network attackers can read OCSP requests sent to https responder URLs on non-443 ports, exposing certificate serial numbers, issuer hashes, and nonces.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118372
CVE.report.description: LibreSSL ocspcheck through 4.4.0 contains a CRLF injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject HTTP headers by embedding CR/LF sequences in a certificate's AIA OCSP URI path. Because url2host() copies the path without rejecting control characters and http_open() places it in the POST request line, attackers can inject headers or split OCSP requests sent to the responder host.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118371
CVE.report.description: LibreSSL through 4.4.0 contains a CRLF injection vulnerability in the libcrypto OCSP_sendreq_new() and OCSP_parse_url() functions, which write unvalidated request paths into the OCSP POST request line. Attackers can embed carriage return and line feed characters in a certificate's Authority Information Access OCSP URI to inject HTTP headers or split requests sent to responders and proxies.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118370
CVE.report.description: libexpat through 2.9.0 contains a signed integer overflow vulnerability in storeAtts() in lib/xmlparse.c that allows attackers to trigger out-of-bounds writes via oversized attribute counts. Attackers can supply a multi-gigabyte document with a start tag carrying over 2^30 attributes to overflow attIndex and nPrefixes, crashing applications or corrupting heap memory.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118274
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability has been found in a2ui-project a2ui up to 0.10.6. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file renderers/web_core/src/v0_9/rendering/generic-binder.ts of the component Binder. The manipulation leads to resource consumption. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The identifier of the patch is c97f4a02d3fea33ce3e9de5cf3fd0e3b8f3a4f0e. To fix this issue, it is recommended to deploy a patch.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118273
CVE.report.description: A flaw has been found in a2ui-project a2ui up to 0.10.6. Affected by this vulnerability is the function DataModel.set of the file renderers/web_core/src/v0_9/state/data-model.ts. Executing a manipulation can lead to resource consumption. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. This patch is called 82789191ce551f4d7a095d273773fb24bd764c9d. A patch should be applied to remediate this issue.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-117610
CVE.report.description: libexpat through 2.9.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in externalEntityInitProcessor2() in lib/xmlparse.c that mishandles the XML_TOK_NONE token from empty input. Attackers who control stream chunking can force an empty non-final first parse on an external entity subparser, causing a later parse to crash the application.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-117609
CVE.report.description: rtl_433 through 25.12 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in proflame2_mc() that allows nearby attackers to write past a 7-byte stack buffer by sending more than seven valid Manchester-coded words. Attackers can transmit a crafted OOK radio signal or supply a crafted signal file to crash rtl_433 and corrupt stack memory, enabling control-flow hijacking on builds without stack canaries.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-117608
CVE.report.description: Assimp through 6.0.5 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in MD2Importer::ValidateHeader() that allows attackers to bypass frame table bounds checks using crafted header fields. Attackers can supply a malicious .md2 file whose numFrames and numVertices values wrap the 32-bit size check, causing heap out-of-bounds reads that crash applications or expose adjacent heap memory.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-117607
CVE.report.description: Xerte Online Toolkits through 3.15.5 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows authenticated users with system permission to run PHP by importing a crafted language pack. Attackers can upload a ZIP via import_language.php containing a .inc file, then request it through the language parameter to execute code on the server.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-117606
CVE.report.description: NexoPOS through 6.3.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated cashiers to manipulate other cashiers' register sessions because CashRegistersService never compares used_by with the user. Attackers holding the default nexopos.use.registers permission can submit closing, cash-in, or cash-out actions to POST /api/cash-registers/{action}/{register} to force-close sessions or alter balances.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-117605
CVE.report.description: nopCommerce before 5.00.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the admin ProductController RelatedProductAddPopup, CrossSellProductAddPopup and AssociatedProductAddPopup handlers that fail to verify parent product ownership. Authenticated vendors can submit another vendor's product id as model.ProductId to inject their products into the victim's related-products, cross-sell and grouped-product listings.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-115624
CVE.report.description: GROWI contains a missing authorization check vulnerability in its collaborative editing feature. By exploiting this vulnerability, a user with read-only permission, including a guest user, or a user in pending, suspended, or invited status may modify page drafts.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-111314
CVE.report.description: The affiliate-toolkit – Multi-Network Affiliate & Amazon Product Display plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'atkp_product_producturl' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.9.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation by unauthenticated attackers requires that the plugin's AJAX loading / AJAX handler option is enabled (atkp_options::get_ajax_loading_enabled() || get_ajax_handler_enabled()) and the attacker knows a product id to render. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-109999
CVE.report.description: The AI Marketing Expert — AI Email Marketing, AI Content Generator, SEO Analyzer, AI Workflow Automation, Social Media & Ai Chatbot plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires only that the chatbot module is active with at least one configured bot; the attacker stores the payload via three unauthenticated REST calls, and the JavaScript widget auto-poll then delivers it to any administrator who opens wp-admin/index.php.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-109974
CVE.report.description: The All-in-One Video Gallery – Video Player & Galleries for YouTube, Vimeo & Self-Hosted Videos plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'more_link' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-109848
CVE.report.description: GROWI contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in its tag update API and the page update API due to improper use of a user-controlled key. By exploiting this vulnerability, an attacker who can log in to the product may obtain the contents of pages without the required read permission and save them to pages that the attacker can edit.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-109209
CVE.report.description: The All-in-One Video Gallery – Video Player & Galleries for YouTube, Vimeo & Self-Hosted Videos plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'custom_fields[embedcode]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The sanitization bypass is possible because the save_meta_data() handler returns early when $_POST['post_type'] is absent — a condition always true during XML-RPC requests — and the plugin unconditionally grants Subscribers the publish_aiovg_videos capability, making this exploitable by any authenticated user via a single wp.newPost XML-RPC call.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-107745
CVE.report.description: The AI Engine – The Chatbot, AI Framework & MCP for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to limited media file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the upload_file function in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.4 This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to delete arbitrary media files on the server. This requires the administrator to have enabled the Public API option, and exploitation depends on the hourly cleanup_files task running after the malicious upload.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-115207
CVE.report.description: A flaw was found in GNU patch. An attacker can achieve arbitrary file creation outside the intended working directory by enticing a user or automated workflow to apply a specially crafted patch file. Due to missing validation during automatic patch reversal, absolute file paths in patch headers are accepted rather than rejected. Consequently, the utility can create files in arbitrary locations with the permissions of the executing user.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114730
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail 1.6.14 before 1.6.20 and 1.7.0 before 1.7.5 is affected by a server-side request forgery filter bypass. The network blocklist used by rcube_utils::is_local_url() omitted the RFC 6052 NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b::/96, the RFC 8215 local-use NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b:1::/48 and the unspecified address ::/128, so URLs such as http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/ passed the filter and reached loopback, link-local and cloud metadata addresses. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix SSRF filter (is_local_url()) bypass via NAT64 64:ff9b::/96”.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114726
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by a mail header injection vulnerability in the Bounce (resend) action. rcube_mime::decode_address_list() did not strip control characters from the decoded display name, so a received message whose From display-name carries CRLF sequences in an encoded word could inject arbitrary headers into the message emitted when the user bounces it. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix mail header injection via the From display-name in the Bounce (resend) action”.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114722
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by a CSS scoping bypass in HTML messages. rcube_utils::mod_css_styles() did not treat an at-rule prologue such as @layer a; as a selector boundary, and did not handle selectors beginning with ::, so selectors following an at-rule were left unscoped and applied to the whole Roundcube interface instead of being confined to the message body. This allows an HTML message to restyle application chrome for UI redressing and spoofing. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix CSS scoping bypass in HTML messages using at-rules”.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114718
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by a cross-site scripting vulnerability in the password plugin. Error text returned by a password driver was concatenated into the message presented to the user without HTML escaping, so a backend able to influence that text, such as the DirectAdmin API, could inject script into the Roundcube interface. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix XSS issue in handling of password driver error responses”, which escapes the driver message before display.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114661
CVE.report.description: OpenRemote 1.2.0 before 1.31.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in GatewayServiceResource that allows any authenticated user to start, stop and query gateway tunnels without an administrative role. Attackers can send POST or DELETE requests to the gateway tunnel endpoint to open persistent bidirectional TCP circuits into an edge gateway's network or tear down operator tunnels.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114657
CVE.report.description: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.5 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows page authors to capture visitors' HTTP Basic credentials through Twig page content. Authors can print the request Uri object, which embeds PHP_AUTH_USER and PHP_AUTH_PW, inside an inline style background image to exfiltrate administrators' credentials to an external host.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114640
CVE.report.description: Traefik from v3.7.0 before v3.7.14 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in its Kubernetes Ingress-NGINX provider that forwards client-supplied Ssl-Client-* headers on the plaintext HTTP router. When ssl-redirect is disabled alongside auth-tls-pass-certificate-to-upstream, unauthenticated attackers can send Ssl-Client-Verify: SUCCESS with a chosen certificate subject and issuer to impersonate mTLS identities.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114636
CVE.report.description: Traefik v3.7.13 before v3.7.14 contains an access-control bypass in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider, where the HTTP router generated for ssl-passthrough Ingresses on non-TLS entry points never applies the Ingress's access-control annotations. Unauthenticated attackers reaching the HTTP entry point with the Ingress host can access backends protected by auth-type, auth-url, or whitelist-source-range annotations, with nothing logged.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114577
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability was found in oretnom23 php-travel-agency-system. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file admin/insert.php of the component Insertion Handler. The manipulation of the argument costomer_id/payment_type/amount/description/user/uploadimage/full_name/visa_no results in sql injection. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-115522 - Cross-Application Artifact Namespace Isolation in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Python
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-115522
Published : Oct. 28, 2026, 4:36 a.m. | 32 minutes ago
Description :Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere (CWE-668) in FileArtifactService in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Python (google-adk) versions 1.19.0 before 1.39.1 and 2.0.0a1 before 2.7.0 allows a caller in one application to list, read, overwrite, or delete artifacts belonging to another application when both applications share a FileArtifactService root directory and use the same user_id (and session_id for session-scoped artifacts). FileArtifactService accepted app_name across its public API methods but omitted app_name when constructing on-disk paths (root/users/{user_id}/... instead of root/apps/{app_name}/users/{user_id}/...). Version 2.6.0 scoped writes by app_name but retained a legacy root/users/{user_id} fallback for reads and deletes; version 2.7.0 and the 1.x backport in version 1.39.1 removed the fallback and enforce full per-app path scoping.
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-104384 - Insufficiently protected credentials in EagleCloud Aquila on-premises version
cvefeed.io Latest.description:

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-50571 - WebSub: Reflected script execution through intent-verification challenges
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-50571
Published : Oct. 27, 2026, 10:40 p.m. | 19 minutes ago
Description :WebSub is a W3C recommendation produced by the Social Web Working Group. In recommendation REC-websub-20180123, the intent-verification protocol requires a subscriber to echo the `hub.challenge` value, also exposed as `hub_challenge` by some frameworks, but does not require safe response media typing or disabled MIME sniffing. An attacker can initiate a subscription to obtain a callback URL and redirect a victim browser to a crafted verification request containing HTML or JavaScript. Subscribers that return the challenge as `text/html` can execute the reflected content in the subscriber origin, using a victim's existing session to read private data or perform actions, exposing `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` and browser permissions granted to that origin. An alternative uses the verification response as an attacker-controlled same-origin script resource to bypass `script-src 'self'`; this can remain possible with `application/octet-stream` when MIME sniffing is allowed. Safe media typing and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` are both needed to address the described scenarios. WebSub Rocks demonstrated reflection, but the advisory does not establish practical impact on that demonstration site.
Severity: 0.0 | NA

Description :Cronicle is a multi-server task scheduler and runner, with a web based front-end UI. Prior to 0.9.121, a non-administrator user or scoped API key with `create_events` and `run_events` privileges can inject top-level `uid` and `gid` fields through `/api/app/create_event` or `/api/app/update_event`. In `lib/api.js`, `requireValidEventData` uses `validateOptionalParams` as a partial allow-list that silently passes unknown keys, storing the injected fields verbatim. In `lib/job.js`, `launchJob` copies the whole event into the job, and a plugin `uid` overrides the event `uid` only when the plugin defines one. The default `shellplug` and `urlplug` plugins do not define a `uid`, so the event-controlled identity survives into child-process launch. On a root-daemon installation, this lets a low-privileged user run jobs as arbitrary users, including root, bypassing the otherwise administrator-only run-as-user control. This API-side event injection is distinct from the job-output `uid`/`gid` injection addressed by CVE-2026-39401. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.121.

cvefeed.io Latest.description:

Published : Oct. 27, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 41 minutes ago
Description :Thor Vector Graphics (ThorVG) is a production-ready vector graphics engine. Prior to 1.0.7, the `SFNT/TTF` font loader's `SfntLoader::gen` function in `tvgSfntLoader.cpp` reads `data[0] through data[3]` to identify the font type without first checking that the input buffer contains at least four bytes. Loading an undersized font directly from memory through public APIs such as `tvg::Text::load` causes an out-of-bounds read. Loading through a file path using `mmap` can mask the read because of page alignment; the memory-loading API directly exposes it. Depending on memory layout, a malformed short font may crash the consuming application or disclose adjacent heap memory. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.7.

External contributors can reach the flaw through fork pull requests only when --allow-fork-prs is enabled, while eligible same-repository branches do not require that option. The commands inherit the Atlantis process environment and can access cloud-provider, Terraform, and version-control credentials as well as files, state, and network resources available to the service. This issue is fixed in version 0.47.1.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-104189 - 3Dviewer-Nextcloud: Share password not enforced when streaming 3D models from a public link share
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-104189
Published : Oct. 27, 2026, 3:22 p.m. | 34 minutes ago
Description :The 3D Viewer for Nextcloud is a comprehensive 3D model viewer application for Nextcloud that supports multiple 3D file formats. In versions 1.7.9 through 3.3.1, the app's public file endpoint performed no share authorization. Anyone who knows a share token could read the shared file's contents even when the link share was protected by a password. `PublicFileController` extended `OCP\AppFramework\Controller` and marked its routes `#[PublicPage]`. Nextcloud only enforces share passwords through `PublicShareMiddleware`, which returns early for any controller that is not an `OCP\AppFramework\PublicShareController` instance — so no password, expiry, or share-type check ran for these routes. `ShareFileService::loadLinkShare()` compounded this by treating any token that `getShareByToken()` matched as authorised. A share token is the part of the URL that people paste into chats, emails, and tickets. Password protection exists precisely for the case where holding the token should not by itself grant access, and that guarantee did not hold. Requests to `GET /ocs/v2.php/apps/threedviewer/public/file/{token}/{fileId}` returned `200` with the full file body for password-protected shares, with no password and no session. Nextcloud's own share page correctly redirected such requests to the password prompt. Scope is limited to files in the formats this app handles (STL, GLB/glTF, OBJ, STEP, IFC, and the other supported 3D types). Non-3D files in the same share are unaffected. Expired shares returned `500` rather than leaking contents. This issue is fixed in 3.3.2. `PublicFileController` now extends `PublicShareController` and implements `isValidToken()`, `isPasswordProtected()`, and `getPasswordHash()`, delegating password and token validation to the framework and gaining brute-force throttling. `ShareFileService::findValidLinkShare()` additionally rejects share types other than link and email, rejects expired shares, and treats a `ShareNotFound` from the share manager as "no share" instead of letting it surface as a 500. As a workaround, disable the 3D Viewer app (`occ app:disable threedviewer`), or avoid relying on passwords to protect link shares that contain 3D model files, until you can upgrade.

Description :The Qode Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.6.2 via the qode_membership_check_facebook_user AJAX action. This is due to a typographic error in the Facebook OAuth token verification guard within the qode_membership_login_user_from_social_network function — the guard condition tests an undefined variable ($check_social_useqoder instead of $check_social_user), causing empty() to always return true and rendering the Graph API token verification branch dead code, leaving wp_set_auth_cookie() reachable with no credential or token validation whatsoever. Exploitation does require harvesting a valid qode_validate_facebook_login nonce, but this nonce is rendered on any public front-end page containing the [qode_user_login] or [qode_user_register] shortcode and is therefore obtainable without any prior authentication.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-110910 - qs.stringify with allowEmptyArrays does not encode the keys of empty arrays, allowing query string parameter injection
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-110910
Published : Oct. 27, 2026, 7:16 a.m. | 1 hour, 41 minutes ago
Description :### Summary `qs.stringify` with `allowEmptyArrays: true` writes the key of an empty array without encoding it, even though keys are encoded by default. A key that contains `&` (or the configured `delimiter`), `=`, or `#` ∴ becomes query string syntax instead of data, so a caller-supplied key name can add parameters to the serialized query string, or cut it short. ### Details In `lib/stringify.js`, the `allowEmptyArrays` branch returns `adjustedPrefix + '[]'` early, before the code that passes every other key through `encoder` and `formatter`. So `{ "x&k=v": ["1"] }` serializes as `x%26k%3Dv%5B0%5D=1`, but `{ "x&k=v": [] }` serializes as `x&k=v[]`. The early return applies at any depth (`{ "a": { "b&k=v": [] } }` gives `a[b&k=v][]`), under every `arrayFormat`, with `allowDots`, and with a custom `encoder`, which is never called for that key. With `encode: false` or `encodeValuesOnly: true`, keys are intentionally left unencoded on every path; those configurations are not affected. #### PoC ```js var qs = require("qs"); var query = qs.stringify({ q: "hi", "x&apiKey=evil&y": [] }, { allowEmptyArrays: true }); // "q=hi&x&apiKey=evil&y[]" qs.parse(query); // { q: "hi", x: "", apiKey: "evil", y: [""] } qs.stringify({ "x#": [], z: "1" }, { allowEmptyArrays: true }); // "x#[]&z=1": in a URL, everything after "#" becomes the fragment ``` #### Fix Applied in 234d505 on `main` and released as v6.17.0: the key of an empty array goes through `encoder` and `formatter` exactly as the key of any other value does, so `{ "x&apiKey=evil&y": [] }` now serializes as `x%26apiKey%3Devil%26y[]`. Keys that need no encoding serialize as before, with two exceptions that match every other path: the brackets of a nested key are now encoded (`a[b][]` becomes `a%5Bb%5D[]`, which `qs.parse` reads identically), and with `encodeDotInKeys`, a dot in the key becomes `%252E` instead of `%2E` (which `decodeDotInKeys` previously misread as nesting). ### Affected versions `>=6.12.0 <6.17.0`, fixed in v6.17.0. `allowEmptyArrays` was introduced in f22b2bc and first shipped in v6.12.0, with this early return. Every release from v6.12.0 through v6.16.1 is affected. Earlier versions have no `allowEmptyArrays` option and are not affected. ### Impact An application that passes an object whose key names come from untrusted input to `qs.stringify` with `allowEmptyArrays: true` (for example, to forward a parsed JSON body or user-selected fields to an upstream service) can have parameters injected into the resulting query string. The injected parameters are not keys of the object, so deleting or overwriting a key on the object (such as setting a trusted `apiKey` after copying the user's fields) does not remove them; whether the attacker's value or the application's wins depends on how the receiving side handles a duplicate parameter. A `#` in such a key ends the query string early when the result is placed in a URL. `allowEmptyArrays` is off by default, and only keys whose value (after any `filter`) is an empty array are affected.
Severity: 6.3 | MEDIUM
Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-110879 - jackson-databind: PolymorphicTypeValidator bypass via generic type arguments and array element types allows arbitrary class instantiation (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-54512)
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-110879
Published : Oct. 28, 2026, 1:16 a.m. | 4 hours, 15 minutes ago
Description :jackson-databind validates the outer class of a class-name type ID but accepts attacker-selected classes inside its generic arguments, even when those classes violate the declared type or would be rejected as direct type IDs. This bypasses the generic-argument validation added for CVE-2026-54512 (GHSA-j3rv-43j4-c7qm), of which this is an incomplete fix. DatabindContext._resolveAndValidateGeneric() checks the outer class against the declared base type and then passes each argument from the type ID to _validateTypeParameter(), which validates the argument against the outer base type rather than enforcing its corresponding declared generic binding. It also invokes validators with arguments that have not passed the subtype check those validators expect. Under the default DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator this accepts an unrelated class inside a generic subtype even when the same class is rejected as a direct type ID. Where an allowIfBaseType(...) rule approves the outer type, Jackson substitutes LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator, so the configured validator no longer restricts the embedded arguments. The element type of a plain array type ID such as [Lpkg.Gadget; is likewise left unvalidated once the array's base type is approved. Affected paths include annotation-based class-name polymorphism with a default Jackson 3.x JsonMapper, configured default typing in both Jackson 2.x and 3.x, and integrations that expose that default typing. The default-validator case requires no application-authored validator: with @JsonTypeInfo(use = Id.CLASS), a direct gadget type ID is rejected as "Not a subtype", while a type ID naming a generic wrapper around the same gadget is accepted and deserialized, including attacker-supplied bean properties. Where class-name default typing permits Map, a property declared as Map accepts HashMap; map-key discovery then passes the attacker-controlled JSON property name to the selected class's one-string constructor. With Spring on the classpath and attacker-controlled XML the application can load, that constructor loads the XML and invokes ProcessBuilder.start() under the application account, giving arbitrary command execution. This issue affects com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 2.10.0 and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 3.0.0. Releases before 2.10.0 are not affected, because PolymorphicTypeValidator was introduced in jackson-databind 2.10.0.
Severity: 9.8 | CRITICAL

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-58255 - Cronicle: Non-admin uid/gid injection in create_event/update_event → run-as-arbitrary-user (incl. root) — sibling of CVE-2026-39401
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-58255
Published : Oct. 27, 2026, 11:17 p.m. | 6 hours, 14 minutes ago
Description :Cronicle is a multi-server task scheduler and runner, with a web based front-end UI. Prior to 0.9.121, a non-administrator user or scoped API key with `create_events` and `run_events` privileges can inject top-level `uid` and `gid` fields through `/api/app/create_event` or `/api/app/update_event`. In `lib/api.js`, `requireValidEventData` uses `validateOptionalParams` as a partial allow-list that silently passes unknown keys, storing the injected fields verbatim. In `lib/job.js`, `launchJob` copies the whole event into the job, and a plugin `uid` overrides the event `uid` only when the plugin defines one. The default `shellplug` and `urlplug` plugins do not define a `uid`, so the event-controlled identity survives into child-process launch. On a root-daemon installation, this lets a low-privileged user run jobs as arbitrary users, including root, bypassing the otherwise administrator-only run-as-user control. This API-side event injection is distinct from the job-output `uid`/`gid` injection addressed by CVE-2026-39401. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.121.

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-112362 - @fastify/express vulnerable to path-scoped middleware bypass via absolute-form request targets
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-112362
Published : Oct. 27, 2026, 12:17 p.m. | 3 hours, 21 minutes ago
Description :@fastify/express is a Fastify plugin that runs Express middleware inside Fastify. In versions 4.0.5 through 4.0.8, when Fastify runs with the non-default ignoreDuplicateSlashes option enabled, the plugin matches path-scoped Express middleware against a URL whose duplicate-slash normalization has also collapsed the separator after an absolute-form request target's scheme, so Fastify's router resolves the request to the scoped path and runs the handler while the Express layer no longer sees that path. As a result, a request using an absolute-form target can reach a handler on a scoped route such as an admin path while the middleware for authentication, authorization, or rate limiting is skipped. An unauthenticated attacker needs only the non-default ignoreDuplicateSlashes option to be enabled. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.9, and users should upgrade to 4.0.9 or later. As a workaround, enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request, or leave ignoreDuplicateSlashes at its default.
Severity: 9.1 | CRITICAL

cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:

Published : Oct. 27, 2026, 9:16 a.m. | 1 hour, 21 minutes ago
Description :The Qode Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.6.2 via the qode_membership_check_facebook_user AJAX action. This is due to a typographic error in the Facebook OAuth token verification guard within the qode_membership_login_user_from_social_network function — the guard condition tests an undefined variable ($check_social_useqoder instead of $check_social_user), causing empty() to always return true and rendering the Graph API token verification branch dead code, leaving wp_set_auth_cookie() reachable with no credential or token validation whatsoever. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in as any existing WordPress account — including Administrator-level accounts — by supplying a known or enumerated administrator login name (rather than an email address) in the response[email] parameter, which the fallback path in get_user_by('login', $email) resolves to the matching account. Exploitation does require harvesting a valid qode_validate_facebook_login nonce, but this nonce is rendered on any public front-end page containing the [qode_user_login] or [qode_user_register] shortcode and is therefore obtainable without any prior authentication.
Severity: 9.8 | CRITICAL

An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability. The ZDI has assigned a CVSS rating of 5.5. The following CVEs are assigned: CVE-2026-93515.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Node.js Brotli Remote Code Execution (Node2Shell)
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Google Brotli decoder, a component used to decompress data encoded with the Brotli compression algorithm. Brotli is widely used in web communications and is bundled with Node.js through its `zlib` module.

Brotli is an open-source project developed and maintained by Google for lossless data compression. It shrinks files so they can be transmitted faster without affecting the original data.

The vulnerability occurs when the decoder processes specially crafted Brotli-compressed input. An attacker who can supply malicious compressed data to a vulnerable application may corrupt adjacent memory, potentially leading to information disclosure, denial of service, or remote code execution.

The root cause is an error in the decoder's handling of malformed block-switch commands. Under certain conditions, the streaming decoder incorrectly treats an invalid block switch as a request for additional input rather than a format error. This can cause data to be written beyond the bounds of an internal eight-byte buffer, corrupting adjacent process memory.

The vulnerability affects Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0. Fixed versions include 1.0.10, 1.1.1, and 1.2.1, depending on the release branch. The Node.js project has also released patched versions for affected release lines.

On October 22, 2026, Imperva published research demonstrating remote code execution against a vulnerable Node.js build. Public proof-of-concept references are also listed in Red Hat's vulnerability bulletin, increasing the risk to unpatched deployments.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Organizations should prioritize updating vulnerable Node.js deployments and Brotli libraries to fixed versions. Because the vulnerability can lead to remote code execution, systems that process untrusted compressed content should receive particular attention.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply security updates: Upgrade Node.js to 22.23.4, 24.22.1, or 26.12.1, as appropriate, or a later fixed release. Update standalone Brotli packages to the applicable fixed version.
2. Review application exposure: Identify services that decompress untrusted Brotli data, including applications using node:zlib, HTTP clients processing compressed responses, and middleware that decompresses incoming request bodies.
3. Apply temporary restrictions where feasible: Until updates are deployed, limit untrusted Brotli-compressed traffic on affected application paths where operationally practical. Test any restrictions to avoid disrupting legitimate traffic.
4. Investigate suspicious activity: Review application and process logs for unexpected crashes or decompression errors. Correlate anomalies with incoming traffic and runtime versions; these symptoms alone do not confirm exploitation.
5. Rebuild and redeploy affected containers: Ensure production images and bundled dependencies include the patched runtime or library rather than relying solely on host-level updates.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs is monitoring CVE-2026-111497 and will update this Threat Signal as new threat intelligence and protection information become available. Organizations should prioritize patching affected Node.js deployments and Brotli libraries, particularly where applications process untrusted compressed data.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

The vulnerabilities affect PHP, a widely used server-side scripting language that powers websites and web applications. They involve flaws in PHP's internal request-processing and memory-management behavior that can be triggered when handling malicious requests. Both are remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities rated as 9.2 (CVSS 4.0).

• CVE-2026-109618 - RCE via out-of-memory corruption: An out-of-memory condition can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Subsequent request-cleanup operations may incorrectly process this invalid data, potentially enabling remote code execution.

• CVE-2026-109619 - RCE via stale global state: Internal request state can persist after its associated memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may access this stale state before normal initialization resets it, potentially enabling remote code execution.

Successful exploitation could compromise the PHP application process and potentially provide access to sensitive server resources, application data, or databases, depending on the permissions of the affected process and the surrounding environment.

PHP announced emergency security updates for October 21, 2026, following reports that details of the vulnerabilities had leaked ahead of the planned disclosure. Subsequent reports highlighted ongoing exploit research and potential attack activity, underscoring the urgency of applying the available patches. However, widespread exploitation of either vulnerability has not been independently confirmed.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

The vulnerabilities affect PHP installations that process web requests, including deployments using PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed. PHP identifies Apache deployments using mod_php as particularly at risk because a demonstrated exploit can trigger before application code runs.

Organizations should prioritize patching internet-facing PHP servers and other exposed deployments immediately.
1. Apply the security updates. Upgrade to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35, as appropriate. Organizations using vendor-maintained packages should apply the corresponding security updates from their distributions or service providers.
2. Reduce exposure until patching is complete. Where immediate remediation is not possible, isolate affected systems from untrusted networks or temporarily disable exposed services when operationally feasible.
3. Review request-processing limits. Apply appropriate web-server or reverse-proxy limits for request sizes, input fields, multipart sections, headers, and nesting depth. These controls can reduce exposure but are not a substitute for patching.
4. Review potentially vulnerable systems. Investigate suspicious web requests, unexpected PHP worker behavior, unexplained process execution, and unusual access to application files or databases. Prioritize internet-facing systems and investigate potential compromise before returning affected services to production.

PHP 8.1 and older are no longer supported by the PHP project and do not receive its standard security updates. Organizations using these versions should check whether their operating-system vendor provides backported fixes or migrate to a supported release.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: OT Refrigeration Control Systems Attack
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

On October 11–12, 2026, attackers compromised refrigeration control systems at supermarkets across France, remotely manipulating refrigeration settings and triggering defrost cycles. The attacks caused temperatures in some refrigeration units to rise to as high as 50°C, resulting in food spoilage and operational disruption. Affected retailers reportedly included Intermarché, Netto, Carrefour, Coopérative U, Monoprix, and E.Leclerc.

France's national cybersecurity agency, CERT-FR, reported compromises involving Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers, as well as Copeland and Dixell XWEB systems. These systems monitor and manage commercial refrigeration and related building operations. Their compromise can allow unauthorized changes to operating parameters, potentially disrupting temperature control and damaging perishable goods.

Separate research by Claroty Team82 identified vulnerabilities affecting Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers, including:
CVE-2025-41450, an authentication bypass
CVE-2025-41451, an OS command injection vulnerability that can lead to remote code execution
CVE-2025-41452, a web server configuration vulnerability that can lead to denial of service
Danfoss released fixes for the above vulnerabilities, and organizations should update affected devices to the applicable patched firmware.

Additional research by Claroty Team82 and CISA documented vulnerabilities affecting Copeland XWEB Pro controllers, including:
CVE-2026-25085, an authentication bypass
CVE-2026-21718, an authentication bypass that can enable pre-authentication code execution
CVE-2026-24663, an unauthenticated OS command injection vulnerability
The affected Copeland models include XWEB300D PRO, XWEB500D PRO, and XWEB500B PRO running firmware version 1.12.1 or earlier. Organizations should consult the vendor's remediation guidance and apply the appropriate firmware updates.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

On October 12, France's national cybersecurity response team, CERT-FR, issued alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 warning of numerous compromises involving remote refrigeration controllers.

Organizations should immediately remove direct internet exposure from refrigeration controllers and restrict remote administration to secure VPN connections or protected management networks. Review controller configurations, particularly temperature settings and defrost schedules, and apply available firmware updates and vendor-recommended security settings. Change default credentials and replace unsupported, end-of-life devices where necessary.

If compromise is suspected, isolate affected equipment and follow vendor and CERT-FR recovery guidance before restoring operations. A factory reset alone is insufficient if the device remains vulnerable and exposed. Organizations should also segment OT networks from corporate IT environments, restrict access to authorized personnel, and monitor for unexpected changes to refrigeration settings.

Danfoss identifies firmware R4.2 as the fix for CVE-2025-41450 and R4.3.1 as the fix for CVE-2025-41451 and CVE-2025-41452. Verify the correct release against the specific device model.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Trimble Cityworks Remote Code Execution Attack
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

Trimble Cityworks contains a deserialization vulnerability. This could allow an authenticated user to perform a remote code execution attack against a customer's Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS) web server, potentially resulting in downtime and potential loss of service.

According to Trimble Cityworks website, it provides a Geographic Information System (GIS)-centric solution for local governments, utilities, airports, and public works agencies to manage and maintain infrastructure across the full lifecycle.

Trimble has investigated customer reports of hackers exploiting the vulnerability to gain unauthorized access to networks, confirming that active exploitation is occurring. CISA has added CVE-2025-0994 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog on February 7, 2025, based on the evidence of active exploitation.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

• The CVE-2025-0994 flaw impacts Cityworks versions prior to 15.8.9 and Cityworks with office companion versions before 23.10.
• Trimble has released updates addressing this deserialization flaw. Ensure these updates are applied to your systems.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs recommends users to apply the fix when provided by the vendor and follow any instructions as mentioned on the vendor?s advisory.
• FortiGuard Labs has blocked all the known malware and related Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) noted on the campaign.
• The FortiGuard Incident Response team can be engaged to help with any suspected compromise.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Atlassian Arbitrary File Access Vulnerability
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack? CVE-2026-21589 is a critical arbitrary file access vulnerability affecting multiple Atlassian Data Center and Server products. It allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access specific files within an affected application's web root, provided the attacker knows the exact file path and name.

The vulnerability stems from improper restrictions on access to files within the web application root. Successful exploitation could expose sensitive files and potentially provide information useful for further attacks, depending on the affected application's configuration and the files accessible.

The vulnerability requires no authentication or user interaction, making internet-facing deployments a priority for remediation.
What is the recommended Mitigation? Atlassian published its security advisory on October 5, 2026, and recommends immediate remediation for affected installations. Atlassian recommends that you patch each of your affected installations to fixed versions or the latest version.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Citrix NetScaler RCE zero-day Vulnerabilities
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

Threat actors are actively exploiting two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances. Citrix confirmed that both vulnerabilities were exploited in the wild before security updates were available. CISA has subsequently added both vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog and reported that threat intelligence confirms exploitation globally.

CVE-2026-88771 is an improper input validation vulnerability that can allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands. It affects NetScaler deployments without requiring an additional feature to be enabled. CVE-2026-88772 is a memory overflow vulnerability that can lead to remote code execution or denial-of-service conditions. It affects appliances with DTLS enabled, which is enabled by default for VPN virtual servers. Both vulnerabilities have a CVSS v4 score of 9.5.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Organizations should immediately identify exposed NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances and apply the security updates provided by Citrix. Fixed releases include NetScaler ADC/Gateway 14.1-73.37 and later and 13.1-64.23 and later, with corresponding updates for FIPS and NDcPP builds.

Because both vulnerabilities were exploited as zero-days before patches were available, patching alone should not be treated as confirmation that an appliance was not compromised. Organizations should review NetScaler and supporting security logs for suspicious activity, preserve forensic evidence where compromise is suspected, and investigate the appliance before making changes that could destroy evidence.

If compromise is suspected, organizations should isolate the affected appliance, review administrative and outbound connections, investigate for persistence, and consider resetting credentials, invalidating sessions, and replacing potentially exposed certificates or keys.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway RCE
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

FortiGuard Labs has observed active network telemetry relating to CVE-2025-7775, a memory overflow vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway that enables remote code execution (RCE) and denial of service (DoS) under certain pre-conditions. Exploitation on unpatched appliances has been confirmed, and CISA has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

Citrix advisories also address:

CVE-2025-7776 – a memory overflow issue causing DoS when NetScaler is configured as a Gateway (PCoIP).

CVE-2025-8424 – an improper access control flaw affecting the management interface.

Recent industry reporting highlights that adversaries increasingly leverage AI-driven exploit development frameworks such as Hexstrike-AI, which integrate large language models (LLMs) with fuzzing and orchestration. These toolchains reduce the time from disclosure to weaponized zero-day exploitation, increasing the urgency for patching.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

The organizations using Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances are strongly recommended to:

- Review and follow the official Citrix security bulletins.
- Apply all relevant patches and updates as soon as possible.
- Monitor for any suspicious activity, such as dropped web shells or abnormal memory behavior.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

  • Intrusion Prevention System (IPS): FortiGuard IPS Service is available to detect and block exploit attempts targeting CVE-2025-7775. Intrusion Prevention | FortiGuard Labs

  • Web Application Security: FortiGuard Web Security Service is available to detect and block exploit activity. Web Application Security | FortiGuard Labs

Fortinet PSIRT Advisories.title: PHP2Shell core RCE vulnerability patches (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)
Fortinet PSIRT Advisories.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 9.8

CVE-2026-109618PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).CVE-2026-109619PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).
